  "title": "The Blind Date",
  "description": "Expanded Series Bible II #31 The Blind Date: two adults knowingly agree to meet as prospective dates knowing little about each other beforehand. The engine generates varied matchmakers, prior information, expectation-versus-reality gaps, venues, situations and open player-facing outcomes.",
  "source_version": "1.1",
  "bible": {
    "series": "Character Card Forge — Series Bible II",
    "series_number": 31,
    "category": "Social Setups & Shared Space (continued)"
  },
  "summary": "Two adults knowingly agree to meet as prospective dates while knowing little about one another beforehand. The recurring engine is the gap between the limited description supplied before the meeting and the actual person who arrives. The description may be incomplete, oddly specific, or entirely accurate but interpreted differently; deception is not required. Matchmakers vary from devoted friends and meddling relatives to apps, professionals and accidents of booking. The reveal can be a dramatic secret, but the strongest variant is often an ordinary but meaningful difference between expectation and reality — a technically true phrase, an outdated file, a familiar face, or no reveal at all. A blind date establishes only that both adults agreed to meet; attraction, chemistry, a second date and how the evening ends all remain open, and {{user}}'s assumptions and reactions are never scripted.",
  "core_premise": "Adult {{char}} and {{user}} have each knowingly agreed to meet the other as a prospective date, arranged by some intermediary and supplied with limited, partial or curated information. The premise opens at or just before the meeting itself, with the gap between the description and the person as the engine: the surprise may come from inaccurate information, omitted context, or a perfectly truthful description that invited the wrong assumption. Deception is not required, and no dramatic secret is needed. Both adults consented to meet and nothing more; whether the evening goes well, badly, hilariously or nowhere is undecided, and {{user}}'s expectations, attraction and willingness to continue are his own.",
  "setup": "Create a non-graphic adult roleplay-card opening around a first blind-date meeting. Establish who arranged it and why, what each participant was told beforehand, where and when the meeting happens, and the concrete gap — subtle or loud — between the description and the adult {{char}} who actually arrives. Give {{char}} a full independent life: occupation, interests, situation, boundaries and her own account of why she is here. If she is attached or has arrangements, let her state them. Open at the arrival, the recognition or the first exchange without writing {{user}}'s dialogue, expectations, feelings or any future outcome.",
  "core_variables": [
    "Who arranged the date: friends, family, classmates, matchmaker, dating service, blind-match app, university event, or another intermediary.",
    "How much each person knows beforehand: first name only, hobbies, occupation, a short description, no photo, partial photo, voice chat, or asymmetric information.",
    "Whether the surprise comes from inaccurate information, omitted context, or a perfectly truthful description that invited the wrong assumption.",
    "Prior relationship: total strangers, distant acquaintances who do not recognise the name, online contacts, or people who have briefly crossed paths before.",
    "What each participant expected from the description versus what actually arrives, without defining {{user}}’s attraction, disappointment, or willingness to continue.",
    "Meeting location and structure: café, restaurant, festival, arcade, university event, hobby venue, or a short planned outing.",
    "Whether the matchmakers genuinely understand both people, are guessing, are meddling, or have accidentally created an unusual but potentially interesting pairing.",
    "How {{char}} herself framed or edited the description: her own words, a friend’s polish, an old profile, a safety-vagued half-truth, or pure accident.",
    "{{char}}’s current situation and commitments: unattached, fresh from a breakup, attached and honest about it, married with her own arrangements, or between everything.",
    "Who {{char}} actually is once she arrives: an ordinary stranger, a hidden specialist, a familiar face, a local personality, or exactly the person described.",
    "The tone of the evening: warm comedy, earnest conversation, awkward near-miss, interrupted chaos, or quiet seriousness.",
    "Whether the outing has a fixed end time, an easy exit, chaperones, observers, or open-ended unallocated hours.",
    "What {{char}} states she wants — serious, casual, unspecified, or undecided — as information rather than an obligation on {{user}}.",
    "Whether a second meeting is scheduled, hinted, refused, or left entirely undecided at the close of the opening.",
    "The gap between description and person is meaningful but ordinary; no dramatic secret or bait-and-switch is required.",
    "{{user}}’s assumptions, attraction, disappointment and willingness to continue are never supplied by the source."
  ],
  "generation_rules": [
    "Do not write {{user}} for the player or define {{user}}'s feelings, decisions, dialogue, consent, intentions, future behaviour, or whether a seduction succeeds unless the source explicitly supplies that fact.",
    "Character belief is not objective truth; keep assumptions, propaganda, cover stories, public records, and objective ground truth distinct where relevant.",
    "Do not pre-play outcomes. Leave cooperation, refusal, forgiveness, exposure, romance, betrayal, joining, leaving, and other player choices open.",
    "All explicit romantic or sexual characters are adults.",
    "Marriage, cohabitation, room sharing, travel, confinement, family relationships, financial payment, and occupational roles do not create romantic or sexual consent.",
    "Sex or intimacy must not erase a character's baseline personality, goals, nonsexual interests, judgement, or boundaries.",
    "Do not require a dramatic secret or bait-and-switch. The strongest blind-date reveal can be an ordinary but meaningful difference between expectation and reality.",
    "A blind date establishes only that both adults agreed to meet as prospective dates. It does not establish attraction, chemistry, a second date, sex, romance, or willingness to remain for the full outing.",
    "Do not define {{user}}’s assumptions unless the source premise explicitly supplies them. NPCs may expect him to be surprised, but his actual reaction remains open.",
    "Overlap boundary: Distinct from Set Up Together because both participants knowingly agreed to a date; Set Up Together remains broader and includes outings that may not initially be understood as dates. Friends’ Blind Date should cross-link here rather than remain a primary Set Up Together subtype.",
    "The matchmakers' competence, motives and honesty should vary: genuinely wise, lucky, careless, meddling, transactional or accidentally brilliant are all valid.",
    "If {{char}} is attached, married or non-monogamous, establish what her actual arrangement is and who within it knows and agrees; an arrangement label is not blanket consent and never obligates {{user}}.",
    "Deception, where present, should have a reason — privacy, safety, humour, carelessness — rather than existing purely for the twist.",
    "Give {{char}} a full life beyond the date: occupation, friends, interests, values and boundaries that exist whether or not the evening succeeds.",
    "The description-versus-person gap should be able to cut both ways: worse than expected, better than expected, simply different, or exactly as promised.",
    "Do not treat 'the date goes well' as the only success state; an honest mismatch, a friendship, a funny disaster or a clean early exit are all valid trajectories.",
    "If a prior connection between {{char}} and {{user}} exists, establish it as pre-scenario history without forcing attraction, resentment or any specific feeling about it.",
    "Keep the opening non-graphic and playable: arrival, recognition, first exchange, disclosure or the moment the gap becomes visible.",
    "Do not preplay {{user}}'s reaction to the reveal, whether he stays, laughs, leaves, asks questions or conceals his surprise.",
    "Wealth, fame, beauty or an unusual lifestyle on either side of the table does not establish moral, romantic or sexual superiority."
  ],
  "guardrails": [
    "All participants in the date, and any partners mentioned within it, are adults.",
    "Agreeing to a blind date is consent to meet only; it is not consent to attraction, sex, romance or staying the full outing.",
    "{{char}}'s own relationship arrangements — open, married, separated — are hers to explain, and no label removes the need for informed agreement from anyone, including {{user}}.",
    "No player reaction is scripted: surprise, delight, disappointment, humour or neutrality all belong to {{user}}.",
    "The matchmakers' enthusiasm does not obligate either participant to enjoy, continue or report back.",
    "A prior connection or past consensual encounter is history, not destiny; it establishes nothing about the present.",
    "Do not require deception; when information was wrong, its source, honesty and consequences vary.",
    "{{char}} retains her own boundaries, pace, occupation, friends and life regardless of how the evening ends.",
    "No predetermined outcomes: second dates, rejection, friendship, revelation or a quiet goodbye are all open.",
    "Intimacy, if it ever develops, is non-graphic at the card stage and requires explicit ongoing consent from adults.",
    "No humiliation, punishment or reward arc is compulsory for either participant.",
    "Keep the premise an engine for many varied cards, not one fixed story."
  ],

    "Arranger identity and motive: devoted friend, bored colleague, wagering flatmates, mothers, grandmothers, apps, professionals or accidents of booking.",
    "Kind of reveal: technically true phrase, outdated file, wrong photo, undersell, oversell, familiar face, hidden speciality, or no reveal at all.",
    "{{char}}'s situation: unattached, recently bereaved or broken up, openly attached, married with stated arrangements, parenting, relocating or mid-reinvention.",
    "{{char}}'s actual world: retro-PC enthusiast, performer, tradeswoman, academic, collector, carer, competitor or ordinary person.",
    "Venue and structure: fixed-booking formality, activity-based casual, outdoor excursion, watched by chaperones, or open-ended hours.",
    "Tone: warm sitcom, earnest slow burn, awkward near-miss, interrupted chaos, quiet seriousness or comedy of assumptions.",
    "Degree of player-facing openness: neutral arrival, stated intentions, disclosed everything, ready to leave, or an open question posed early.",
    "What the opening leaves undecided: a second date, an exit, a walk after, a confession or simply the last sip of coffee."

  "raw_prompt": "Generate a non-graphic adult character-card premise for The Blind Date. Two adults knowingly agree to meet as prospective dates arranged by an intermediary — friends, family, a matchmaker, an app or an accident — knowing little about each other beforehand. The engine is the gap between the description supplied in advance and the adult {{char}} who actually arrives: technically true phrases, omitted context, outdated files, wrong photos, familiar strangers, hidden specialities or no reveal at all; deception is not required. Vary the arranger's motive and competence, the venue and structure, {{char}}'s situation and commitments, and the evening's tone. Agreeing to meet is consent to meet only — no attraction, second date, intimacy or outcome is predetermined, and {{user}}'s assumptions, reactions and choices are never written. All participants are adults; consent, boundaries and player agency remain open."
